headline: FrogNano-4B Q8_0 re-run at 128K context — the highest context window that comfortably fits in a 12 GB 3080 Ti. Model + Q8_0 KV cache = 10,699 / 12,288 MiB (~87%), single slot, fully on GPU, ~164 tok/s. This is the context-ceiling test: same model/quant/scores as the 16K entry, only the context window changed. Every number below was read from the live machine (nvidia-smi / lms ps) at load time.
hardware: box strata (retired Oct 2026): RTX 3080 Ti 12 GB — LM Studio
facts: Answer: what is the highest context window FrogNano-4B Q8_0 comfortably fits in 12 GB VRAM? Bracketed with lms load --estimate-only, then verified with real loads + nvidia-smi.

64K=8,267 MiB (67%) · 96K=9,483 MiB (77%) · 128K=10,699 MiB (87%) · ~140K≈11.5 GiB (94%, tight) · 160K=12,400 MiB (estimate, WILL NOT LOAD) · 256K=16,830 MiB (way over). Ceiling is ~140-150K; 128K is the highest round value with headroom.
frognano-4b-2609 — bartowski/FrogNano-4B-2609-GGUF Q8_0 (imatrix), 5.29 GB on disk, 4.93 GiB runtime (lms ps). Base: microsoft/FrogNano-4B-2609 (4.66B, Qwen3.5-4B, RL-trained coding agent, MIT).

Objective: fib/constraints/json all PASS (10). Subjective: reasoning 9, creative 8, breakout 2 (BROKEN this run), delta 6, fractal 5. Composite 6.9 — dragged down by a genuine breakout regression vs the 16K run.

breakout: TWO fatal JS bugs — (1) draw() is called on page load (line 505 'Initial Draw') BEFORE initBricks(), so bricks[0][0] throws 'Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 0)'; (2) paddleX is declared const (line 187) but reassigned in resetBall()/movePaddle() -> 'Assignment to constant variable'. Result: canvas stays 0% painted even after clicking Start. Unplayable. A real variance/regression vs the 16K run's polished breakout (9).

observations.text: Same model, quant, and scores as the 16K entry — the ONLY variable is context window. tok/s is identical (~164). The one difference in results is a genuine per-run coding variance: breakout was a polished 9 at 16K but is broken (2) at 128K, and the two game defects flipped (fractal now renders Mandelbrot cleanly, breakout regressed). That variance is exactly what the benchmark surfaces.

open: The two FrogNano rows (16K and 128K) differ only in context window; the score delta is run-to-run coding variance, not a context effect.
